title.en: Nissan, the month of renewal

summary.en: The Mashgiach opens with the idea that a Jew can renew himself and that the world was created in Nissan. Nature sleeps through the winter and wakes in Nissan as a kind of techiyas hameisim, which is why the haftarah of the dry bones is read on Pesach.

title.en: Salvations circling; rebirth of nature and nation

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains the piyut's words that salvations circle in Nissan like birds, and that the spring rains fill the empty pits, as spiritual flow fills empty people. Since what happens in heaven shows itself below, the rebirth of the Jewish people at the Exodus is mirrored in the rebirth of nature, and Nissan brings a flow of love and chesed.

title.en: Shir HaShirim and the song of Nissan

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains why Shir HaShirim is said on Pesach: Nissan pours love and song onto all of creation, and each person chooses where to direct them; Shlomo HaMelech caught that song for Hashem. Everything opens in Nissan, the treasury of tal included, and among the things that open is the Jewish heart, to which Hashem calls 'kol dodi dofek, pischi li'.

title.en: Pischi li: 'my head is filled with tal'

summary.en: The Mashgiach compares Nissan to the opening of the aron, an eis ratzon when the Zohar's Brich Shmei is said, and explains that Hashem knocks on each Jew's heart and asks him to open because He comes with gifts: His head is filled with tal. Through the gematria of the Name with its milui he shows that tal is the flow of blessing, and calls on the listeners to wake from the sleep of winter to the true sweetness of Torah.

title.en: Vayikra's small aleph: no chance

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that Vayikra opens with a language of chibah because Hashem is close, a relative of the Jewish people. Amalek is the power of 'mikreh', chance, and Adar is a time of hester panim; the small aleph of Vayikra is seen only from close by, while one who is far reads 'vayikar', coincidence. In Nissan a Jew draws near and sees that Hashem runs everything.

title.en: Matzah as 'patir', the key that opens

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings that the Targum calls matzah 'patir', from 'peter rechem', an opening; matzah is a key to the blessings of tal on Pesach night. He brings the Targum Yonasan that the gates of heaven opened on the night Yaakov took Yitzchak's blessings, suggests this is the source of stealing the afikoman, and says matzah opens the heart, which is why the door is opened for Eliyahu.

title.en: Nissan's chesed and the kingship of Hashem

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that Nissan's tzeruf is 'yismechu hashamayim vesagel ha'aretz', the Name in its straight order, pure chesed, so its avodah is through song, matzah and kindness, as Hilchos Pesach opens with maos chittin. Nissan is Rosh Hashanah for kings and the time the nation was created, which answers why the Aseres HaDibros say 'who took you out of Egypt'; he hopes for the day when even the nations will say 'Hashem malach'.

title.en: Nissan holds the whole year

summary.en: The Mashgiach tells that the Ba'al Shem Tov secluded himself on Rosh Chodesh Nissan, and contrasts Nissan's aleph-beis in order with Tishrei's reversed order. He brings from the Bnei Yissaschar the story of the Chozeh of Lublin, who on each of the first twelve days of Nissan wrote down all that would happen in one month of the year, since each day of the Nesi'im leads a month.

title.en: Searching out the chametz of the heart

summary.en: The Mashgiach divides Nissan's avodah into 'sur mei'ra', removing chametz, and 'aseh tov', eating matzah. He asks why the Torah is so strict with chametz and answers from the Zohar that chametz is the yetzer hara, so one must search the holes and cracks of the heart by the light of the soul. He tells how the Lechovitcher Rebbe sent a messenger to announce this on the night of bedikas chametz.

title.en: Matzah, the food of emunah, against Amalek

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that the Zohar calls matzah 'michla dimeheimnusa', the food of emunah. Erev Pesach is a war against Amalek, whose gematria is 'safek', doubt: burning the chametz burns the yetzer hara, and eating matzah brings in emunah. He compares matzah to a capsule whose hidden ingredient strengthens a Jew for the whole year.

title.en: Ha lachma anya: the same matzah as in Egypt

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Satmar Rav on the Magen Avraham's question how one can say 'ha lachma anya': the matzah's physical form is only a container, and its inner light is the same as in Egypt, so 'this night is all matzah'. He explains 'kulanu mesubin' as everyone having cheirus, and tells of the Yismach Moshe, who was shown Eliyahu offering korbanos, and of a tzaddik who felt the korban Pesach in his afikoman.

title.en: Matzah, the holy Names, and leaning on it

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings that matzah equals three times the Name with its milui, higher than ordinary bread, which equals three times the Name and is sanctified by netilas yadayim and hamotzi. Eating matzah takes the holy Names into oneself. He then brings the Midrash that even a poor man must recline, and asks how one may lean on the afikoman under the pillow when one may not lean on a sefer.

title.en: Leaning on Hashem: simcha and its opposite

summary.en: The Mashgiach answers that matzah is emunah and bitachon, and a Jew leans on Hashem. Simcha, with sin that sounds like samech, comes from 'somech', leaning, while atzvus comes from 'azuv', forsaken. Rich and poor have the same Ribono shel Olam to lean on; one who relies on Him is not shamed, while 'kesufas panim', the pale face of shame, is a sign of chametz.

title.en: Avraham Avinu and the spring of every Jew

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that Pesach is the yom tov of Avraham Avinu, to whom everything happened on Pesach, the first of the believers. Pesach is a time of techiyas hameisim; a Jew must not be worse than a tree that blossoms, but sprout and bear fruit through the mitzvos of Pesach. He closes with a tefillah for the Nissan of the complete redemption.

catalogTitle: חודש של חידוש ואהבה

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach explains Nissan as the month of renewal and chesed, and matzah as the key that opens a Jew to emunah and to a bond with Hashem beyond time and place.

abstract.en: Following Rabbi Yehoshua that the world was created in Nissan, the Mashgiach traces three Nissans of creation: the world itself, spoiled by Adam's sin; Klal Yisrael at the Exodus, spoiled by the Golden Calf; and the Mishkan, a smaller world of holiness. The final Nissan will be the redemption. Hashem did not tire of renewing, and a Jew should not either. Nissan is the month of chesed, the right side, against Tishrei's din. Spring, described in Shir haShirim, calls on the Jew to renew himself along with creation. Matzah is the key: the Targum calls it 'petira', opening, and Pesach is about opening doors and the heart. Pesach is Avraham's festival and the foundation of emunah, the time to plant faith in children. Matzah is heavenly food beyond time and place, holding the Divine names. The Mashgiach closes with the Radbaz that chametz is the yetzer hara, two stories, and a call to pray for a kosher Pesach.

en: Nissan is the month of creation, renewed three times: the world, Klal Yisrael at the Exodus, and the Mishkan; the final renewal will be the redemption.
Nissan is the month of chesed, the right side, while Tishrei is the month of din.
Matzah is the key to Nissan: the Targum calls it 'petira', opening, and all of Pesach is about opening up.
Pesach is the festival of Avraham Avinu, the first of the believers, and so it is the foundation of emunah.
Matzah is a heavenly food above time and place, unlike chametz, which time acts on and which spreads in space.
Bread lives through the 'word of Hashem' within it; matzah carries the full Divine name three times, and the one who eats it absorbs emunah.
Pesach is the lowest of the festivals but their foundation, the bond of a Jew with Hashem, and one must pray for a kosher Pesach.

title.en: The three Nissans of creation

summary.en: Following Rabbi Yehoshua that the world was created in Nissan, the Mashgiach shows how the world, then Klal Yisrael at the Exodus, then the Mishkan were each created in Nissan, the first two spoiled by sin, with the final Nissan of the redemption still to come. From Hashem renewing again and again, and from the Mishkan set up seven times, he learns not to give up after a failure.

title.en: Nissan, the month of chesed

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that the world was built with chesed and that Nissan is the month of chesed, the right side, which Jews strengthen in many customs. He contrasts Rabbi Yehoshua and Beis Hillel (chesed, Nissan) with Rabbi Eliezer and Beis Shammai (din, Tishrei).

title.en: Spring calls the Jew to renew himself

summary.en: Pesach opens with chesed, and in Nissan the whole world renews itself, as Shir haShirim describes the spring. The Mashgiach asks the Jew why he alone should stay old when all of creation rises anew, and ties this to the haftarah of the dry bones.

title.en: Matzah, the key that opens

summary.en: The Mashgiach calls matzah the key to Nissan: leaving the narrowness of Mitzrayim, the Targum's 'petira' meaning opening, opening the door at the seder, and the storehouses of dew opened on Pesach night. Pesach calls on a Jew to open his heart, and the Maharal explains that spring renews nature because Klal Yisrael is renewed.

title.en: Pesach, Avraham's festival of love and emunah

summary.en: On Pesach everything is renewed, house, clothes and dishes, and a Jew should ask Hashem to renew him. The Mashgiach shows that Pesach is Avraham's festival: his bris, the angels' visit and his war with the four kings were all on Pesach, and as the root of love and of emunah he makes Pesach the foundation of emunah.

title.en: Planting emunah in the children; eating emunah

summary.en: Pesach is the festival of the children and the time to plant emunah in them, simply and in their language. Talking about emunah is not enough; one must eat it, and matzah, the 'food of faith', becomes part of the person's flesh and blood.

title.en: Matzah above time and place

summary.en: Everything in this world exists in time and place, as the laws of witnesses show. Matzah is heavenly bread that time does not rule; once eighteen minutes of time act on dough it becomes chametz and spreads in space. Emunah likewise means believing in what is beyond grasp.

title.en: The soul within bread

summary.en: The Mashgiach asks how physical bread can give life, and answers from the passuk that a person lives by the 'word of Hashem' in the bread, its soul. Bread holds three times the name Havayah, and a Jew who washes and makes hamotzi for the sake of Heaven eats that holiness into himself.

title.en: Matzah, the full Divine name, and 'Mah'

summary.en: Matzah equals three times the name Havayah spelled out in full (45), the miraculous source of the Exodus beyond understanding. The seder is full of the word 'mah', the question with no answer, which is emunah. The Mashgiach tells how the Divrei Chaim, after the seder, felt the holy names absorbed into his body.

title.en: Pesach the foundation; chametz is the yetzer hara

summary.en: Pesach is the lowest of the festivals but their foundation, the bond with Hashem, which is why its prohibition carries kares. The Mashgiach brings the Radbaz that chametz is the yetzer hara, to be uprooted entirely, and tells of Baron Rothschild's 'Pesach house' and the Divrei Chaim's answer that Hashem wants the chametz removed and matzah brought into the same place.

title.en: Praying for a kosher Pesach

summary.en: Pesach cleaning is uprooting the yetzer hara, and one must pray for a kosher Pesach. The Mashgiach tells of a tzaddik who found a wheat kernel in his soup at the seder and learned from Heaven that he had not prayed to be saved from chametz, then explains the two eatings of matzah as the past and future redemption and closes with a blessing.

catalogTitle: התעוררי "תחיית המתים" ביחד עם העולם!

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach explains Nissan as the month of chesed and renewal, when the world and Klal Yisrael are created anew, and calls on everyone to rise to a 'techiyas hameisim' of fresh life in learning, davening and eating mehudar matzah.

abstract.en: Opening on Shabbos Parshas HaChodesh, the Mashgiach explains that Nissan is a time of midas hachesed, when the Name of Hashem stands in its straight order. He brings the dispute of Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Yehoshua whether the world was created in Tishrei or in Nissan, and Tosafos that both are true. Next year's Birkas HaChamah will fall on erev Pesach, so great times are coming. Nissan renews all of nature, unlike Tishrei, and Pesach is a time of techiyas hameisim: one must not be 'dead' in learning and davening. The first twelve days of Nissan govern the year, as the story of the Chozeh of Lublin shows. Matzah is the food of emunah; by gematria it is three times the full Name of Hashem, three times 'adam'. Chametz is the yetzer hara, so one should eat mehudar matzah baked lishmah, ideally chaburah matzos, and be careful about every trace of chametz.

en: Nissan is a time of midas hachesed, when the letters of Hashem's Name stand in their straight order; in Tishrei they are reversed, which is midas hadin.
In Nissan all of nature is renewed, and Pesach is a time of techiyas hameisim; the Mashgiach calls on the bochurim to rise with freshness and life in learning and davening.
Each of the first twelve days of Nissan governs one month of the year, so one should daven on them with life and enthusiasm.
Matzah is the 'food of emunah', and by gematria it equals three times the full Name of Hashem, three times 'adam', while ordinary bread equals only three times the simple Name.
Chametz is the yetzer hara, which is why the Torah is so strict about it, and burning and cleaning chametz removes the yetzer hara from a person.
Matzah must be baked lishmah because holy Names are in it, and so the Mashgiach urges mehudar matzah, ideally chaburah matzos, at least for the sedarim.

title.en: Nissan, the month of chesed and creation

summary.en: The Mashgiach opens with Parshas HaChodesh and Rosh Chodesh Nissan, explaining that in Nissan the Name of Hashem stands straight, which is chesed. He brings the dispute whether the world was created in Tishrei or Nissan and Tosafos' answer that both are true.

title.en: Birkas HaChamah and great times ahead

summary.en: The Mashgiach notes that next year Birkas HaChamah will be said in Nissan, on erev Pesach, as in the year of yetzias Mitzrayim, and warns that great times are coming and life cannot go on as usual. He mentions the coming Pesach and the Purim meshulash in Yerushalayim, and urges holding on to the inspiration.

title.en: Nissan renews nature; Tishrei is its opposite

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that the world was built with chesed and that in Nissan Hashem created Klal Yisrael. He paints the spring: warm winds, returning birds singing new songs, green fields and flowers, contrasted with Tishrei's falling leaves, and reads 'aviv' as alef-beis in order against Tishrei's letters going backwards.

title.en: Pesach as techiyas hameisim

summary.en: The Mashgiach describes how everything becomes new for Pesach, and brings the brachah 'mechayeh hameisim' on something not seen for twelve months. Pesach is techiyas hameisim, as the haftarah of the dry bones shows, and he calls on the bochurim to rise up with freshness in learning and davening.

title.en: The first twelve days of Nissan and the Chozeh

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings a tzaddik's reading of 'lo amus ki echyeh' about people who are dead while alive. He explains that the first twelve days of Nissan govern the twelve months, tells the story of the Chozeh of Lublin's notebook as brought by the Bnei Yissaschar, and urges davening with chiyus on these days.

title.en: Matzah, the food of emunah, and its gematria

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Zohar that matzah is the 'food of emunah', notes how rare true emunah is in our generation, and explains that eating matzah is eating holy Names. Bread equals three times the simple Name of Hashem, but matzah equals three times the full Name, three times 'adam', explaining 'lo al halechem levado yichyeh ha'adam'.

title.en: Why chametz is so strict; mehudar matzah

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings Tosafos' question why chametz has so many stringencies, the Rishonim's disputed answers, and the Radbaz that the only answer is that chametz is the yetzer hara. From here he urges eating mehudar matzah baked lishmah, explaining why Chassidic gedolim did not allow machine matzos.

title.en: Matzah in place of tefillin; chaburah matzos

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that on Chol HaMoed Pesach the matzah takes the place of tefillin, so it deserves the same care. He praises chaburah matzos baked with joy, brings the Bnei Yissaschar's lesson from the dor haflagah that repeating 'l'shem' adds holiness, and says the matzah annuls the power of Klal Yisrael's enemies.

title.en: Care on Pesach and closing blessing

summary.en: The Mashgiach says Avraham fought the kings on Pesach night with the power of matzah, then urges great care with even a trace of chametz, bringing the Arizal that this guards a person from sin all year and the Mishnah's language about the korban Pesach. He closes with a blessing for the coming blessed days and the full redemption.

catalogTitle: The Candles Glow with the Light of משיח

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach explains that the Chanukah candles reveal the hidden light of creation and the light of Moshiach, and shows how Moshiach ben Yosef was hidden in the story of Dina, Shechem and Osnas, a spark of holiness concealed in the lowest place.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with the hidden light of the first day of creation, which Adam used for thirty-six hours and which Hashem hid in the Torah; it is found in the thirty-six tractates of Shas and in the thirty-six Chanukah candles. Bringing the Rokeach and the Bnei Yissaschar, he explains that the Chanukah light also reveals the light of Moshiach, which is why Chanukah has eight days. Moshiach comes in two stages, Moshiach ben Yosef, who fights Esav, and Moshiach ben David. He then tells, from the Targum Yonasan, how Osnas, the daughter of Dina and Shechem, came to marry Yosef, and shows that the seed of Moshiach ben Yosef was hidden in Shechem, like a diamond hidden in a garbage can. Like the Chanukah candle, which is lit below ten tefachim on the side of the Satan, Dina went down to draw holiness out of impurity. He ends with the wonders hidden in every word of Torah.

en: The hidden light of the first day, which Adam enjoyed for thirty-six hours, is hidden in the Torah and comes down to us in the thirty-six Chanukah candles.
The Chanukah light reveals the light of Moshiach, and Chanukah has eight days because eight belongs to Moshiach, above the seven of the natural world.
Moshiach comes in two parts: Moshiach ben Yosef, who wages the war against Esav, since Esav falls only to the children of Rachel, and then Moshiach ben David.
Hashem hides the roots of Moshiach in the lowest places, like a diamond hidden in a garbage can, so that the Satan should not look for it there.
The Chanukah candle is lit below ten tefachim and on the left side, the domain of the Satan, to find holiness there and draw it up, which is the way of Moshiach.
Dina was born to bring Moshiach ben Yosef into the world; she went out like the Chanukah candle into the domain of impurity to draw out holiness.

title.en: The hidden light and the thirty-six candles

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that the hidden light of the first day, which Adam used for thirty-six hours thanks to Shabbos, was hidden in the Torah, and that it comes down in the thirty-six tractates of Shas and the thirty-six Chanukah candles.

title.en: The light of Moshiach and the number eight

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Rokeach on the thirty-six mentions of light in the Torah and the extra crowns on the first tes, and the Bnei Yissaschar that the Chanukah light reveals the light of Moshiach. This is why Chanukah has eight days: eight, like the eight-stringed harp of the future, belongs to Moshiach.

title.en: Moshiach ben Yosef and the war against Esav

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that Moshiach comes in two parts, Moshiach ben Yosef and Moshiach ben David, and that Esav falls only to the children of Rachel. He relates the Chafetz Chaim's words about three wars, mentions the protection of seudah shlishis from the war of Gog and Magog, and says that both lights of Moshiach glow in the Chanukah candles, in Hallel and in Al Hanisim.

title.en: The story of Osnas, daughter of Dina

summary.en: From the Targum Yonasan and the Da'as Zekeinim, the Mashgiach tells how Yaakov saved the child of Dina and Shechem, angels brought her to Egypt, Potiphar adopted her, and Yosef recognized her by his father's note on her necklace and married her.

title.en: A diamond hidden in a garbage can

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that Shechem carried a spark of Moshiach ben Yosef, hidden there as one hides a diamond from thieves in the garbage. He brings the Chasam Sofer that Dina went out to draw holiness out of the people of the land, and adds that she was sent out so that Moshiach ben Yosef, the adversary of Esav, should come out.

title.en: The candle in the domain of the Satan

summary.en: The Mashgiach contrasts the Gemara that the Shechinah never came down below ten tefachim with the Chanukah candle, which is lit below ten tefachim and on the left side, the side of the Satan. Chanukah goes down into his domain to find holiness and draw it up, and this, he says, is the meaning of Moshiach, who goes down to the lowest depths to bring up the Jews.

title.en: Yehuda, Yosef and Ovadia: treasures below

summary.en: The Mashgiach shows that in the parshiyos of this week both Moshiach ben David, from Yehuda and Tamar, and Moshiach ben Yosef, from Yosef's descent, come out of low places. He brings Ovadia, a convert from Esav, who prophesies Esav's fall, like the axe handle taken from the forest, and announces that he will share wonders from the parshiyos of Kislev and Teves.

title.en: Why Dina: the exchange with Yosef

summary.en: The Mashgiach asks why Dina of all people was to bring Moshiach ben Yosef, and answers from the Targum Yonasan and Rashi that Yosef was first conceived by Leah and Dina by Rachel, so Dina, originally Yosef, provided Yosef's match. He adds that the letters of Dina spelled out in full equal in gematria Moshiach ben Yosef.

title.en: Dina in the box, the hidden Chanukah light

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that Dina is the Chanukah light, born to go down into impurity and bring out Moshiach. Rashi's account of Yaakov hiding her in a box from Esav, because of Leah's debt to Esav, is no accident: she belongs concealed like the hidden light. He ends with a story of the Avnei Nezer showing wonders in every piece of Torah and with the passuk asking Hashem to uncover the eyes to see them.

catalogTitle: חטוף כח החידוש מהסיטרא אחרא

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach explains why the frog's song in Perek Shirah is 'Baruch shem kevod malchuso', a quiet praise from the place of mixed good and evil, and how the sitra achra has seized the power of renewal that belongs to the Jewish people in Nissan.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with Nissan, when all creation is renewed and sings, and brings Perek Shirah, where the frog tells King David that its song is greater than his. He asks why, and brings the dispute of Rabbi Akiva and Rabbi Elazar ben Azaryah over 'one frog'. Building on the Bnei Yissaschar, who ties the frog to the attribute of yesod, he explains that the frog lives both in water and on land and is a mixture of tahor and tamei. Therefore its song is 'Baruch shem kevod malchuso', said quietly, because it declares Hashem's rule even in the place of the sitra achra. Tumah begins with 'two', as the tractates Ohalos and Negaim open with 'shnayim'. In the future, says the Imrei Emes, Baruch shem will be said aloud, and the frog merited this through mesirus nefesh. He then explains that renewal belongs to the Jews; when they neglect it the sitra achra seizes it, as seen in modern inventions that take away a Jew's peace. He calls for fresh avodah and stronger yiras shamayim.

en: The frog, which lives both in the sea and on land, is the intermediate between tahor and tamei and a mixture of good and evil.
The frog's song in Perek Shirah is 'Baruch shem kevod malchuso', praise that comes from the place of the sitra achra and is therefore said quietly.
Kedushah is oneness and tumah is division, which is why Ohalos and Negaim, the severest forms of tumah, open with the word 'shnayim'.
In the time of Moshiach Baruch shem will be said aloud, and the frog's song, earned through its mesirus nefesh, will be the highest of all.
Renewal belongs to the Jewish people; when they do not use it, the sitra achra seizes it, as with the flood of modern inventions.
Today's test cannot be escaped, so ordinary, traditional yiras shamayim is not enough; one must strengthen it and serve Hashem with freshness.

candidateTopics: kedushah as oneness and tumah as division

title.en: Nissan: all creation sings

summary.en: The Mashgiach opens with Nissan, the month of renewal, when creation sings to Hashem, and describes Perek Shirah, where each creature praises Hashem with a passuk. He notes the two songs of Nissan, the Hallel in Egypt and the song at the sea, and that the future song will be a 'shir chadash'.

title.en: The frog's song and 'one frog'

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the opening of Perek Shirah, where a frog tells King David that its song is greater than his, and asks how that can be. He then brings the dispute of Rabbi Akiva and Rabbi Elazar ben Azaryah over 'one frog' and asks why Rabbi Elazar ben Azaryah sent him specifically to Negaim and Ohalos.

title.en: The frog and the attribute of yesod

summary.en: The Mashgiach sharpens the question: he could have sent him to monetary law or to Kodshim. He brings the Bnei Yissaschar that the plagues correspond to the ten sefiros and the frog to yesod, and explains that Pharaoh wanted to keep the Jewish girls alive to create a mixture of good and evil, which the Avnei Nezer says is worse than evil itself.

title.en: The frog between tahor and tamei

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings that every kind on land has a counterpart in the sea, one tahor and the other tamei, and the principle, from Rabbi Pinchas of Koretz via the Bnei Yissaschar, that between two extremes there is an intermediate. The frog, found both in the river and on land, is that intermediate, a mixture of tahor and tamei, and so it punished the Egyptians who sought to mix.

title.en: Why Baruch shem is said quietly

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Gemara that Yaakov answered his sons' Shema with Baruch shem, and that it is said quietly like the king's daughter who craved a lowly dish. He explains that Shema is the higher unity of Hashem who is wholly holy, while Baruch shem declares that His rule extends even to the lowest places of the sitra achra, which is true but unseemly to say aloud.

title.en: The frog sings Baruch shem

summary.en: The Mashgiach shows that in Perek Shirah the frog's song is Baruch shem. Since Hashem does not want praise from the wicked, a tamei creature's song is said by its tahor counterpart, but the frog, itself a mixture, sings quietly, and it alone sings no passuk. He adds the Midrash that the destroyers flee from Shema and whisper Baruch shem, and explains why one says Baruch shem after a needless brachah.

title.en: Tumah begins with 'two'

summary.en: From the Rambam's order of the tractates the Mashgiach shows that Ohalos and Negaim are the severest tumah. Kedushah is oneness and tumah is division: the second day brought Gehinnom, pairs are dangerous, and Yeravam made two calves. Ohalos and Negaim open with 'shnayim', which resolves the dispute: the frog is a mixture of one and two. He adds the shuruk, the vowel of yesod, behind 'eshreka lahem'.

title.en: Baruch shem in the future

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Imrei Emes that in the future Baruch shem will be a passuk and be said aloud, and explains that once all tumah is gone, as with the Midrash that the chazir will become tahor, Hashem's rule everywhere will no longer be a disgrace. The Midrash reads 'tzefardea' as 'tzipor de'ah', tied to 'the earth shall be full of knowledge', and the frog's song will then shine.

title.en: The frog's mesirus nefesh

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that the frogs gave their lives for Hashem by jumping into the ovens, and that the path of yesod is mesirus nefesh, as Yosef HaTzaddik earned his level through his test. He quotes the Imrei Emes and the Belzer Rebbe that before Moshiach nothing is achieved without mesirus nefesh, defines it as giving up one's will, and concludes that the frog's song will be the finest because of its mesirus nefesh.

title.en: Renewal belongs to the Jews

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that the avodah of Nissan, 'hachodesh hazeh lachem', is to serve Hashem every day as if for the first time. He brings the Chiddushei HaRim that renewal belongs to the Jews, and when they neglect it the sitra achra seizes it, as in 'a new king arose over Egypt', and the Avnei Nezer that the nations have festivity because the Jews did not keep Shabbos as a day of menuchah.

title.en: Rabbi Elazar ben Arach

summary.en: The Mashgiach tells of Rabbi Elazar ben Arach, the greatest student of Rabbi Yochanan ben Zakai and a soul with a spark of Moshiach, who went to the ten tribes to bring them back, was drawn after them and forgot his learning, reading 'hachodesh hazeh lachem' as 'hacharesh haya libam'. He explains that he grasped the passuk of his root, the first mitzvah tied to Moshiach, and lamented that their hearts did not hear the call of renewal.

title.en: The sitra achra's new inventions

summary.en: The Mashgiach applies 'a new king who did not know Yosef' to our time, when the renewal of Yosef has passed to the sitra achra through new devices such as the internet and television. He describes how the world lived unchanged for centuries until a sudden power of renewal came down, which first showed in great Torah giants and the Ba'al Shem Tov, but the Jews did not seize it and the nations did.

title.en: How the new devices steal menuchah

summary.en: The Mashgiach describes how the telephone, then the cellphone, and the airplane took away a Jew's peace and time for learning, so that the sitra achra uses the renewal meant for chiddushim in Torah. He says the Jews must be renewed, not asleep, and points to the haftorah of the dry bones read on Pesach.

title.en: Two kinds of test

summary.en: The Mashgiach distinguishes the test of keeping away from evil, as the nazir is told to go around the vineyard, from the greater test of being trapped inside it, as Yosef was. He tells a story from the Chazon Ish of a Jew whose ordinary yiras shamayim failed when an important guest was due on Friday night, and concludes that in our generation one must strengthen one's yiras shamayim.

title.en: Renewal in learning and davening

summary.en: The Mashgiach calls for new 'inventions' in the war against the yetzer hara: learning with life, davening with feeling, and finding a good minyan. He notes the second day of Pesach and the haftorah of the dry bones, and closes with a tefillah to sing the new song with Moshiach and to say Baruch shem aloud.

catalogTitle: לעזור בבית בהכנה לפסח; להתחדש עצמו בזמן התחדשות

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach teaches that the lowly work of cleaning before Pesach is precious to Hashem, and that Nissan, the month in which all of creation is renewed, calls on every Jew to renew himself through emunah and to begin again.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with the terumas hadeshen, the removal of the ashes at night, and explains that this humble night avodah, done in work clothes, is most dear to Hashem; so too taking a broom and helping at home before Pesach, as a story with Rav Gifter shows. He then turns to Nissan, the month of creation. Hashem tried four times in Nissan to bring the world to its tikkun: at creation, at Yetzias Mitzrayim, at the Mishkan, and the Nissan of the geulah still awaited. Hashem does not give up, and a Jew too must always begin again. In Nissan all of nature comes back to life, and the Jew is called to renew himself. The key is matzah, which is emunah: in Hashem, in the chachamim and in oneself. Nissan asks a person to become an adam by ruling over the animal of his own mazal. Avraham Avinu, whose Yom Tov is Pesach, is the spring of Klal Yisrael. The Mashgiach closes with a story of Reb Arele Roth.

en: The terumas hadeshen, a night avodah done in work clothes, is most precious to Hashem, and it is the model for the humble work of cleaning and helping at home before Pesach.
Hashem tried in Nissan to bring the world to its tikkun at creation, at Yetzias Mitzrayim and at the Mishkan, and a fourth Nissan of geulah is still to come.
Just as Hashem does not give up, a Jew must always begin again, whenever he falls.
In Nissan all of nature is renewed, and a Jew is called to see himself as part of that renewal.
The key to renewal is matzah, which is emunah: in Hashem, in the chachamim, and in oneself.
To become an adam, each person must know which animal of his mazal he is and ride it rather than let it ride him.
Avraham Avinu, the first Jew and the spring of Klal Yisrael, has Pesach as his Yom Tov, and the emunah he began is taught to children at the seder.

matzah as the bread of emunah

title.en: Terumas hadeshen and helping before Pesach

summary.en: The Mashgiach asks why the Torah waits until Tzav to speak of the olah, and explains that the night avodah of removing the ashes, done in work clothes, is the most precious to Hashem, like the avodah of the generation before Moshiach and like sweeping the house before Pesach. He tells how Rav Gifter came himself to take out a couple's garbage.

title.en: Nissan creation and birkas hachamah

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the dispute of Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Yehoshua whether the world was created in Tishrei or Nissan, and that birkas hachamah follows Nissan. As an aside he brings the Ostrovtzer's calculation that it fell on erev Pesach only at the Mishkan and at the time of Purim, and will again at the geulah, and suggests why those were times with little to prepare.

title.en: Four Nissans of tikkun

summary.en: The Mashgiach describes Hashem's plan for a perfected world, spoiled by the sin of Adam HaRishon in Nissan; the second attempt, Yetzias Mitzrayim and Matan Torah, spoiled by the eigel; the third, the Mishkan, which was later destroyed; and the fourth Nissan of geulah that Hashem has promised.

title.en: Always beginning again

summary.en: From Hashem's repeated attempts the Mashgiach draws the lesson that a Jew must always start anew: like a jigsaw puzzle taken apart and begun again, like the tzaddik who falls seven times and rises, every Shabbos, Rosh Chodesh and morning. He adds that Hashem Himself, as it were, asks for a kaparah for diminishing the moon.

title.en: All of nature is renewed in Nissan

summary.en: The Mashgiach describes, through Shlomo HaMelech's words in Shir HaShirim, how the dead winter gives way to buds, birdsong and fragrance in Nissan, because then Hashem renewed His bond with Klal Yisrael. A Jew who sees all of creation renewed must ask whether he is part of that song, and Hashem knocks and calls him to rise.

title.en: Matzah, emunah and the key to renewal

summary.en: The Mashgiach calls Nissan the key to a new creation and says the key is matzah, which is emunah. He explains Moshe Rabbeinu's sin at the rock as a lack of faith in himself, and brings Rav Hirsch's three kinds of emunah. He explains why the Targum calls matzah 'petir', opening, and how the seder opens and closes with opening.

title.en: Becoming an adam: souls and mazalos

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that Nissan is the time of 'na'aseh adam' and demands that each person become an adam, but says each must answer for himself how. He brings the Tikkunei Zohar on Esther's plea to save her soul from the dog: souls come from different roots and mazalos, compared to animals, as the shevatim are compared to animals.

title.en: Riding one's own animal

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that each person's yetzer follows his mazal, and that the soul must rule over its animal like a rider. A young man born under the lion who rises easily to learn has nothing to boast about; his test is not to tear at others. Each person must assess which animal he is, ride it, and renew himself in this Nissan.

title.en: Avraham Avinu, the spring of Klal Yisrael

summary.en: The Mashgiach shows that Avraham Avinu, the first Jew, is the spring of Klal Yisrael and that Pesach is his Yom Tov: the bris bein habesarim, his milah and his victory over the kings all fell on Pesach. Emunah, Avraham's trait, is the first of the Aseres HaDibros, is taught to small children at the seder, is eaten in the matzah, and, as the Maharal says, is the essence of tefillah.

title.en: Reb Arele and the Chanukah lights; closing

summary.en: The Mashgiach urges using the days before Pesach for learning and davening with simchah, and brings Reb Arele Roth's teaching that there is no such thing as not being in the mood. He tells how the gravely weak Reb Arele lit the Chanukah lights with all his strength and danced before the doctor, and closes with a wish that this Nissan be the Nissan of the geulah.

catalogTitle: דרוש בענין: זמן של חודש ניסן הוא הנקודה האמצעות שבשנה

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach explains that Nissan, the month of chesed and of the Exodus, is the central point and root of the whole year, just as the Beis Hamikdash is the point from which the world grew and 'darosh darash Moshe' is the center of the Torah.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with emunah as the root of all mitzvos and with the Ramban's teaching that every mitzvah is a remembrance of the Exodus, so Pesach is the root of all the festivals and Nissan the head of the months. He brings the dispute of Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Yehoshua whether the world was created in Tishrei, with din, or in Nissan, with chesed. He then explains the halacha that a rebellious elder is liable only in the Lishkas HaGazis: the world grew from one point, the foundation stone, and the Sanhedrin sitting there holds the power of the root. The middle of Sefer Devarim and the middle of the Torah, 'darosh darash Moshe', mirror this. That verse concerns the Rosh Chodesh Nissan goat that was burned, which the Mashgiach explains through the diminished moon and the kushyos on Hashem, all to be answered in the days of Moshiach, a preview of which Aharon earned through his silence. He closes with the Chozeh of Lublin and with strengthening emunah in Nissan.

en: Since all mitzvos are a remembrance of the Exodus, Pesach is the root and 'embryo' of all the festivals, and Nissan the head of the months.
According to Rabbi Yehoshua the world was created in Nissan, a renewal of chesed, while Rabbi Eliezer holds it was created in Tishrei, with the attribute of din.

The world developed from a single point, the foundation stone in the Holy of Holies, which is why the Beis Hamikdash is called higher than all places and why the Sanhedrin's ruling has full force only there.
The Torah is the blueprint of the world, so its center, 'darosh darash Moshe', corresponds to Rosh Chodesh Nissan, as the word Bereishis corresponds to Tishrei.
The goat of Rosh Chodesh is an atonement 'for Hashem' for the diminishing of the moon, Knesses Yisrael, and for all the questions people have on Hashem's conduct.
The Rosh Chodesh Nissan goat was burned because that day was a preview of the days of Moshiach, when it will be revealed that Hashem never needed atonement.
Nissan builds the whole year through chesed and love rather than through din, and at the root of the year one should strengthen the mitzvah of emunah.

title.en: Emunah, the Exodus and the head of the festivals

summary.en: The Mashgiach opens with emunah as the root of all mitzvos and the Ramban's teaching that every mitzvah recalls the Exodus, which showed that Hashem runs the world. Therefore Pesach is the head and the embryo of all the festivals, and Nissan the head of the months.

title.en: Nissan, a renewal of chesed

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the dispute whether the world was created in Tishrei or Nissan and explains Nissan as a renewal of chesed, seen in spring and explained by the Maharal as Hashem renewing His bond with Klal Yisrael. He contrasts chesed, giving outward, with din, drawing inward, through the order of the letters, and ties Tishrei to din and Nissan to chesed.

title.en: The rebellious elder and 'the place causes'

summary.en: The Mashgiach reads the passage of the rebellious elder in Parshas Shoftim and the Gemara's lesson that 'the place causes': the elder is liable only for defying the Sanhedrin in the Lishkas HaGazis. He stresses how central one final authority is for Klal Yisrael and asks how the Beis Hamikdash can be called higher than all places.

title.en: The world grew from one point

summary.en: Since the world is round, no point on it is simply highest; but its Maker began it from one point, the foundation stone, and wound it outward like an embryo, through the Beis Hamikdash, Yerushalayim and Eretz Yisrael. The Torah is the world's blueprint, the heads of the generations are its central souls, and the Sanhedrin sitting at the root point has the strongest power, which is why 'the place causes'.

title.en: The center of Sefer Devarim

summary.en: Sefer Devarim repeats the whole Torah and so contains the blueprint of the world; its middle verse, by the count of the Masorah, is in the passage of the Sanhedrin, corresponding to the Beis Hamikdash at the world's center. He adds Sefer Yetzirah's three dimensions of place, time and soul, whose holiest points meet when the Kohen Gadol enters the Holy of Holies on Yom Kippur.

title.en: Bereishis and 'darosh darash Moshe'

summary.en: According to Rabbi Eliezer the root of the Torah is the word Bereishis, matching Tishrei and din, whose service is that of the Kohen Gadol; according to Rabbi Yehoshua it is 'darosh darash Moshe', the middle of the Torah in words, matching Nissan and Moshe Rabbeinu the king. He adds a teaching on the word 'saraf' as the six hundred thousand interpretations of the Torah.

title.en: The burned goat and the diminished moon

summary.en: The middle of the Torah speaks of the goat brought on Rosh Chodesh Nissan, the eighth day of the Mishkan's inauguration, which was burned. The Mashgiach explains the Gemara that the Rosh Chodesh goat is an atonement 'for Hashem' for diminishing the moon: the moon, Knesses Yisrael, receives from the sun, the earth's physicality comes between them, and Klal Yisrael will be renewed like the moon.

title.en: Kushyos on Hashem and the root of roots

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that the questions people raise against Hashem, while Klal Yisrael is diminished and mocked, are what the Rosh Chodesh atonement addresses. Rosh Chodesh Nissan is the root of all the months, and on that eighth day a preview of the days of Moshiach was revealed, when all questions will be answered and it will be clear that Hashem needs no atonement; therefore that goat was burned.

title.en: Aharon's silence and the Jewish renewal

summary.en: The preview was earned through Aharon's silence after his sons died: he could have asked questions but believed without understanding. The Mashgiach contrasts the nations, who have a year of repetition, with Jews, who have a month of renewal and teshuvah, calls Rosh Chodesh Nissan a time of atonement, and explains that Nissan's new year works through chesed, a new year for the kings.

title.en: The Chozeh's pinkas and the root of the year

summary.en: The Mashgiach tells, from the Bnei Yissaschar, how the Chozeh of Lublin would write on each of the first days of Nissan what would happen in the matching month, and one year stopped before the day of Av, the month he passed away. He concludes that Nissan, built with chesed, is the root of the whole year, holding the days of Moshiach and the center of the Torah, and calls for strengthening emunah, the root of all mitzvos.

catalogTitle: 8 Days Ruled by the Timeless Light of משיח (connection to פרשת וישלח)

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach explains that the eight days of the Chanukah miracle were one long day in the Mikdash, a glow of the light of Yemos HaMashiach that stands above the seven-day order of time.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with the Gemara that wicks and oils unfit for Shabbos may be used for Chanukah, and explains that the light of Chanukah reaches souls that Shabbos cannot ignite. Chanukah is a foretaste of Yemos HaMashiach, when the seven-stringed harp of the Mikdash will have eight strings. Time is built of seven days, while Moshiach will be above time. He notes the strange wording of the Beraisa and the Mechaber, 'on the 25th of Kislev the days of Chanukah are eight', which the Rama corrects with 'begin'. He asks how the Kohanim could fulfil the mitzvah with miraculous oil, and answers that in the Mikdash the eight days were one long day, so the first lighting stretched over all eight. This explains why Chanukah is named for the 25th, why the Kohanim cried and then stopped, the word 'mitzvah' in Haneiros Halalu, and how Hashem moved the nature of the future into that time. He closes that Chanukah is a time of thanking Hashem, above all for being a Jew.

en: Wicks and oils that do not burn well on Shabbos may be used on Chanukah, because the light of Chanukah reaches souls that Shabbos cannot ignite.
Chanukah is a foretaste of Yemos HaMashiach, the eighth string beyond the seven notes of the present world.
Time is built of seven days, while the light of Moshiach, from which the Chanukah miracle came, is above time.
In the Mikdash the eight days of the miracle were one day eight days long, so the Kohanim did not have to light again.
Chanukah is a time of thanking Hashem, and above all for being a Jew, which is what the Chanukah war was fought for.

the eighth string of the harp

title.en: Chanukah light for souls Shabbos cannot ignite

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Gemara that wicks and oils unfit for Shabbos may be used for Chanukah, and explains that the Shechinah comes down on Chanukah to souls that Shabbos cannot ignite. He then calls Chanukah a foretaste of Yemos HaMashiach, when the seven-stringed harp will have eight strings.

title.en: Above time: 'the days of Chanukah are eight'

summary.en: The Mashgiach says time is built of seven days while Moshiach will be above time, and Chanukah too is not bound by the order of time. He points to the difficult wording of the Beraisa and the Mechaber, 'on the 25th of Kislev the days of Chanukah are eight', which the Rama corrects by adding 'begin'.

title.en: Can a mitzvah be done with miracle oil?

summary.en: The Mashgiach asks how the Menorah could be lit with oil that refilled miraculously, since such oil is not olive oil squeezed from olives. He brings the Derech Pikudecha that a mitzvah cannot be done through a miracle, and describes the Kohanim crying over it.

title.en: Time in Yemos HaMashiach and the eighth note

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that in Yemos HaMashiach the order of time will change and days will be like years, comparing it to the year of the Mabul when the constellations did not function. Creation follows seven notes, as the seven days and the seven mizmorim of Kabbalas Shabbos show; Moshiach will bring an eighth, Binah, and the Chanukah miracle was a glow of that light above time.

title.en: One day eight days long in the Mikdash

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that Hashem gave the Mikdash one day that lasted eight days, so the Kohanim's first lighting continued and they did not need to relight; the Chashmonaim's mizmor ending 'orech yamim' alludes to this. This answers the Beis Yosef's question why all eight days are called by the name of the 25th, and the wording without 'begin'. He then asks why the Kohanim stopped crying if the stretched day were not so.

title.en: The Menorah above and the stretched mitzvah

summary.en: With the parable of two pianos, the Mashgiach explains that whatever is done below registers above: the Menorah burning in the Mikdash below meant the Menorah above was burning, and the Kohanim cried for fear of darkness in the world. The miracle was that the single lighting remained a mitzvah, which explains the word 'mitzvah' in Haneiros Halalu, kept by the Ba'al HaTanya, and he concludes that Hashem moved the nature of Yemos HaMashiach into the time of the Chashmonaim.

title.en: Chanukah's blessing: thanking Hashem

summary.en: The Mashgiach says each Yom Tov has its own blessing to take along, and that of Chanukah is hallel and hoda'ah; the Rambam waits until the laws of Chanukah to give the laws of Hallel. He calls for a cheshbon hanefesh of all Hashem's kindnesses, and above all thanks for being a Jew, since on Chanukah the Jews fought for Torah, Shabbos, Rosh Chodesh and milah.

catalogTitle: “בקש הקב"ה לעשות חזקיהו משיח...” זמן לעבוד על אמונה בהשגחה פרטיות

oneLiner.en: Starting from the Gemara that Hashem wanted to make Chizkiyahu Moshiach, the Mashgiach explains why salvation must be met with shirah and thanks, and why Nissan and Pesach are the time to plant emunah in Hashem's hashgachah pratis behind every event.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with the Gemara that Hashem wished to make Chizkiyahu Moshiach, but he did not sing shirah after the fall of Sancheirib. Linking this to Chizkiyahu's intercalating Nissan on the thirtieth of Adar, he explains that Chizkiyahu felt he was fit to be Moshiach but not yet appointed, and held back for the sake of souls not yet ready, as the Ohev Yisrael said in a story. He then turns to the war against the Yishmaeli king of Bavel, which was won in Nissan while Jews read the nesi'im, and shows connections to Yosef, Yishmael and chametz. Through Achashverosh, a king who crowned himself, he shows that Hashem saves through unworthy agents, and calls for shirah and thanks, bringing the Chasam Sofer. The second half teaches that the Megillah and Pesach are for learning hashgachah pratis, contrasting it with Amalek's 'mikreh', and ends with Moshiach standing on the roof of the Beis HaMikdash once Amalek is gone.

en: Chizkiyahu did not sing shirah because he felt he was fit to be Moshiach but not yet appointed, and a shirah then would have been the tenth song of the final redemption.
The redemption waits until all souls of Klal Yisrael are ready, including the 'Adar souls' pushed out of the order.
Hashem brings salvation even through an unworthy king, like Achashverosh who crowned himself, to show that He alone is the One who saves.
After a salvation there is an obligation to say shirah and to thank Hashem, learned by kal vachomer from the shirah at the Yam Suf.
The Megillah, thirty days before Pesach, teaches hashgachah pratis: a Jew must believe now that everything is for the good of Yisrael, not only understand it afterwards.
Amalek's heresy is that everything is chance, and its poison can only be cured by hearing the story of Yetzias Mitzrayim from a true tzaddik, as Yisro did and as Jews do on Pesach night.

Yishmael in the end of days
Nissan as the month of redemption
Moshiach on the roof of the Beis HaMikdash

title.en: Why Chizkiyahu did not sing shirah

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Gemara in Sanhedrin that Hashem wanted to make Chizkiyahu Moshiach but held back because he did not sing shirah, and asks why such a tzaddik did not. He adds the Gemara in Berachos that Chizkiyahu joined geulah to tefillah and intercalated Nissan on the thirtieth of Adar, and later regretted it.

title.en: The tenth shirah and the souls of Adar

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings that there are ten shiros in the world, the tenth belonging to Moshiach, and explains that Chizkiyahu feared that his shirah would seize the role of Moshiach before he was appointed, just as he held that 'fit to be Nissan' is not yet Nissan. He ties this to Nissan and Moshiach both being called 'rishon', and to souls of 'Adar' who still await their tikkun.

title.en: The Ohev Yisrael and the waiting for all souls

summary.en: The Mashgiach tells that the Ohev Yisrael said he could bring Moshiach but would not, since some souls would be lost, and answered a Rav who objected. Chizkiyahu felt the same; the redemption waits until all souls are ready, which is why the earth's wish to sing was answered with 'razi li'.

title.en: The war with the Yishmaeli king of Bavel

summary.en: The Mashgiach describes the great salvation Jews just had from the Yishmaeli ruler in Bavel who boasted he would destroy Eretz Yisrael and spread fear everywhere. He brings the Zohar and Targum Yonasan that the twelve nesi'im subdue the twelve princes of Yishmael, and notes that the war turned in Nissan while Jews read the nasi and did bedikas chametz.

title.en: The ten makos, Yishmael and se'or

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that pouring out wine at the ten makos at the Seder subdues the enemies of Yisrael, and that Rabbi Yehudah's simanim also hint at the Yishmaelim, who began the galus by selling Yosef, as Rashi says about Pinchas's war with Midyan. He suggests that chametz is the other nations and se'or, which is not fit to eat, is Yishmael.

title.en: Victory on the day of Efrayim's nasi

summary.en: The Mashgiach notes that Baghdad fell on the seventh day of Nissan, the day of the nasi of Efrayim, a descendant of Yosef, who embodies holy bris milah against Yishmael's empty milah. He brings the Ba'al HaTurim that when Yishmael falls Moshiach will come from Yitzchak's children, and concludes that Jews must say shirah on Shevi'i shel Pesach.

title.en: A king who crowned himself

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Gemara that Achashverosh became king on his own, and the Maharal on why the Torah does not name Moshe's parents: the redemption is not because of anyone's worthiness. Hashem uses unworthy agents to show that He saves, and the Mashgiach applies this to the American president and to the Stoliner Rebbe's prediction that America would help Jews in danger.

title.en: Shirah after a salvation: the Chasam Sofer

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Gemara's kal vachomer that shirah after a salvation is rooted in the shirah at the sea. He tells how in the Chasam Sofer's city the battle with Napoleon's forces spared the Jews, compares it to the Gulf War's missiles, and relates how the Chasam Sofer ordered tefillos during the war and chapters of Tehillim of thanks after it, as written in his Sefer HaZikaron.

title.en: Thanking Hashem for every small thing

summary.en: The Mashgiach teaches that thanking Hashem for every small thing is a foundation of a Jew, with the story of a Lithuanian Jew praised by the Chozeh of Lublin and of Rav Yonasan Steif thanking Hashem for a breeze. He suggests that perhaps the redemption waits for our shirah and proposes that shuls set a time on Shevi'i shel Pesach to say the Chasam Sofer's chapters of thanks.

title.en: A salvation both sweet and bitter

summary.en: The Mashgiach tells how the Chasam Sofer, thanking the Kaiser for granting Jews freedom, wept and gave a mashal of a banished prince who cries when the king builds him a comfortable house in exile. So too the present salvation is sweet but bitter: Jews hoped the wars were Gog and Magog leading to Moshiach, and instead they have menuchah in galus.

title.en: An os l'tovah and the Megillah read backwards

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Ibn Ezra that Esther delayed her request to wait for a sign for good, which came with Haman's downfall before Mordechai, and suggests the present salvation may be such a sign, a sprouting of the redemption in Nissan. Everything that happens is for the good of Yisrael; one who believes it only after the end of the story is like one who reads the Megillah backwards.

title.en: Vayikra versus vayiker: providence or chance

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that the Megillah, thirty days before Pesach, comes to teach hashgachah pratis against Amalek's belief in 'mikreh', chance. Through Rashi on the small aleph of Vayikra he contrasts the heretic who says the world 'happened' with the Jew who knows everything was called into being by Hashem, and he connects 'asher karcha' of Amalek with Haman's story.

title.en: The Ruzhiner and the natural Yam Suf

summary.en: The Mashgiach asks why Yisro came after hearing of kriyas Yam Suf and Amalek, as Rashi says, if he already knew. He tells of a heretic who told the Ruzhiner that the splitting of the sea had natural causes, and the Ruzhiner's answer that such a once-in-history convergence at exactly the right moment would be an even greater nes, a hidden one like Purim.

title.en: Amalek's poison and the antidote of Pesach night

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that Amalek attacked because he held the sea split by itself, and that Yisro, hearing this, was poisoned by his heresy; even passing words of apikorsus are a contagious poison. The antidote was to hear Yetzias Mitzrayim from Moshe Rabbeinu, and so Pesach night, when Yetzias Mitzrayim is the root of emunah, is the time to plant emunah.

title.en: The world is a Megillah

summary.en: The Mashgiach teaches that the whole world is a Megillah in which Hashem's name is hidden, and that Haman saw miracle after miracle and still called it chance. He brings the Chasam Sofer that the gentile chronicles credit Achashverosh's might, while Jews know Hashem did it all, and the Chasam Sofer's answer why the miracle was at the sea and not at the Nile: so that Jews could make a brachah on the place of the nes.

title.en: Moshiach on the roof; Shiloh without a roof

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Pesikta that Moshiach will stand on the roof of the Beis HaMikdash, and asks why on the roof. Through the Gemara in Zevachim that Shiloh had stone walls and a roof of curtains, he explains that the roof corresponds to heaven and to keser, and that because Amalek, whose gematria is 'ram', is the head of the sitra achra, the roof could not hold kedushah.

title.en: Wiping out Amalek and the holy roof

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Gemara that before building the Beis HaMikdash Amalek must be wiped out, and shows that each time Amalek was only weakened, so the roof remained without kedushah. In the third Beis HaMikdash, with Amalek and the pride he brings gone, Moshiach, called 'rishon', will stand on a holy roof, and the Mashgiach closes with the hope of Nissan as the month of redemption.

catalogTitle: חודש של זריזות והתחדשות

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach teaches that Nissan is a month of chesed and renewal in which Hashem's original plan for the world is tried again, and that its blessing is received only through zerizus, the alacrity of matzah, as opposed to the lazy rising of chametz.

abstract.en: Opening with Parshas HaChodesh, the Mashgiach calls Nissan a month of chesed and of zerizus: heaven pours out kindness, and a person without alacrity is a bucket with a hole. Zerizus is learned from matzah. He then explains that the world was created in Nissan for a life of sweet closeness to Hashem, like an endless spring, and Avraham Avinu is the spring of Yiddishkeit. Adam spoiled the plan; Hashem tried again with the Exodus, spoiled by the Golden Calf, then with the Mishkan, spoiled by the foreign fire; the fourth Nissan, the final redemption, will succeed. The Mishkan set up seven times teaches that one who falls must rise again rather than let things go chametz. Pesach is a rebirth, like nature's spring. A story of a poritz who spread sugar on his field to sled in summer contrasts with the sweetness of a Jew's Shabbos. He ends urging zerizus in davening and learning.

en: Nissan is a month of chesed, and only one who receives it with zerizus keeps the blessing that pours down.
Zerizus in all mitzvos is learned from matzah, which must be baked quickly so it does not become chametz.
Hashem created the world in Nissan so that man would live in Gan Eden in the sweetness of closeness to Him, and Nissan is the month in which that plan is tried again.
The plan was tried in four Nissans: at creation, at the Exodus, at the Mishkan, and in the coming redemption, which will not be spoiled.
Chametz is the bread of laziness, puffed up with air and emptiness, while matzah is the bread of zerizus.
Pesach is the greatest Yom Tov because through it one became a Jew; it is a rebirth, like the spring that revives the dead world of winter.

title.en: Nissan: a month of chesed and zerizus

summary.en: The Mashgiach opens with Parshas HaChodesh and its piyut on the blessed days that are coming, and calls Nissan a month of chesed in which a person must set out a bucket without a hole. He explains that Nissan is a month of renewal and zerizus, learned from the quick baking of matzah.

title.en: The world created in Nissan for sweetness

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Gemara's dispute whether the world was created in Nissan and explains Hashem's intention: a world like Gan Eden where man enjoys the sweetness of closeness to Him, a sweetness Jews can taste in davening. He describes spring in detail and calls Avraham Avinu the spring of Yiddishkeit, then says Adam spoiled the plan.

title.en: The second and third Nissan: Exodus and Mishkan

summary.en: Noting that the shivas yemei hamiluim begin today, the Mashgiach explains that Hashem tried His plan again in a smaller form with the Jewish people leaving Egypt, which was spoiled by the Golden Calf, and again with the Mishkan erected on Rosh Chodesh Nissan, which was spoiled by the foreign fire.

title.en: The fourth Nissan: the final redemption

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings Chazal that in Nissan the future redemption will come, and says the fourth Nissan will not disappoint: the whole world will serve Hashem and the nations will stream to the third Beis HaMikdash. He says one must prepare for Nissan with kedushah and Torah.

title.en: Rising after a fall; chametz as laziness

summary.en: The Mashgiach notes that the parshiyos of the Mishkan's inauguration are read at this season, and that the Mishkan was set up and taken down seven times before it stood, like a tzaddik who falls seven times and rises. One who falls must not let things go chametz: chametz is the bread of laziness, rising only with air, while matzah is the bread of zerizus.

title.en: Pesach: Avraham's Yom Tov and rebirth

summary.en: The Mashgiach recalls baking matzos with joy and song, and brings the Zohar that matzah is the food of emunah. Pesach is Avraham Avinu's Yom Tov, when his great events took place, and the greatest Yom Tov because through it one becomes a Jew. He paints winter as death and spring as tchiyas hameisim, the theme of the haftarah of the dry bones, and asks why a Jew should stay asleep.

title.en: The poritz who sledded on sugar

summary.en: The Mashgiach asks when a Jew will take up avodas Hashem with zerizus and feel a pleasure no gentile can buy. He tells of a poritz who, in August, had sacks of sugar spread over his field so he could ride his sled, and contrasts that poor pleasure with what a Jew feels saying Nishmas on Shabbos morning.

title.en: Shabbos sweetness and the call to zerizus

summary.en: The Mashgiach describes the sweetness of Shabbos and brings the Beis Aharon that a blatt Gemara before davening is Gan Eden. He closes urging his listeners to use the time, rise early, come early to davening, and treat these days as the miluim, a training like the kohanim, who are zerizim, in preparation for the coming Nissan.

catalogTitle: צד א: הקדמה ללימוד מהר"ל. יצ"מ התגלות הקב"ה; ביאור עמוק שבנ"י הם ההיפוך של מצרים.

oneLiner.en: After introducing the Maharal as the key to Chazal's aggados, the Mashgiach begins Gevuras Hashem: yetzias Mitzrayim is Hashem's revelation and the foundation of emunah, and Klal Yisrael, like Avraham from Ur Kasdim, had to begin from Mitzrayim, their exact opposite.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens by explaining that the aggados of Shas hide deep wisdom and cannot be read by their plain meaning, citing the Ramchal. The Maharal was chosen from Heaven to explain them through pure, simple logic rather than pilpul, and all streams of Klal Yisrael built on him. The Mashgiach describes the Maharal's sefarim, recommends starting with Nesivos Olam and Derech Chaim, and announces that he will teach the main ideas of Gevuras Hashem before Pesach. He then begins: the Ramban at the end of Parshas Bo makes yetzias Mitzrayim the foundation of all emunah, and the Maharal says Hashem chose that night to make His deeds known. Klal Yisrael reached completeness at six hundred thousand, like a body with six sides. Mitzrayim was the exact opposite of Yisrael, and only from the opposite, from zero, can a true beginning come, as with Avraham from Ur Kasdim and his break from Terach.

en: The aggados of Shas are not to be read literally; they hide deep wisdom like a code, and the Maharal was the one who opened them through clear logic.
The Maharal's way is depth and simple truth, not pilpul or clever constructions, and one must get used to it over time.
Following the Ramban at the end of Parshas Bo, yetzias Mitzrayim is the foundation of the whole Torah and of emunah, since there Hashem revealed Himself to a whole nation.
Klal Yisrael became a complete nation only at six hundred thousand, since six marks completeness, like a body with six sides.
Mitzrayim was the exact opposite of Klal Yisrael, and that is what made it the deepest galus.
A true beginning must start from zero, from the opposite; so Avraham came out of Kasdim and Yisrael out of Mitzrayim.

title.en: The hidden wisdom in Chazal's aggados

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that each generation's sages had their own portion in Torah, and that the aggados of Shas cannot be read by their plain meaning. Citing the Ramchal, he says they hide deep wisdom like a code, and that the secrets of the Torah lie in them.

title.en: The Maharal, key to the aggados

summary.en: The Mashgiach presents the Maharal as the one chosen to explain the aggados through deep, simple logic rather than pilpul, accepted by Chassidim and the mussar movement alike. He lists the Maharal's sefarim, advises beginning with Nesivos Olam and Derech Chaim, and explains why gedolim called his mind a 'sechel nivdal', a mind free of personal bias.

title.en: Preparing for Pesach with Gevuras Hashem

summary.en: The Mashgiach notes that Gevuras Hashem was the Maharal's first printed sefer and tells of a chassid whose Pesach preparation was learning hilchos Pesach and Gevuras Hashem. Since people are busy, he announces he will present a digest of the sefer before Pesach and asks for patience in getting used to the Maharal's style.

title.en: Yetzias Mitzrayim, the root of emunah

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Ramban at the end of Parshas Bo that yetzias Mitzrayim is the foundation of all of Torah and emunah, and the Maharal's opening that Hashem chose that night to make His deeds known. He ties this to the mitzvah of Anochi, the zecher l'yetzias Mitzrayim of the Yamim Tovim and the daily mention of the Exodus.

title.en: Six hundred thousand: a nation complete

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that the Jewish people was formed at yetzias Mitzrayim once it reached six hundred thousand, since six is the number of completeness: a point, a line and a flat area are incomplete until there are six sides. He then brings 'goy mikerev goy', that Yisrael were taken out of Mitzrayim like a fetus from its mother.

title.en: Mitzrayim, the exact opposite of Yisrael

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that Mitzrayim, the land of immorality, was the exact opposite of the holy nation, so being strangers there was the deepest galus. He brings the story of Rabbi Yochanan ben Zakkai and the daughter of Nakdimon ben Gurion and the Maharal's explanation of 'ashreichem Yisrael': the lowness of their galus shows how high Yisrael are.

title.en: Beginning from zero: Avraham and Ur Kasdim

summary.en: The Mashgiach compares yetzias Mitzrayim to Avraham leaving Ur Kasdim, a people that 'was not'. Avraham, the purpose of creation, came at the end of the two thousand years of tohu, because a beginning must start from zero; so too Yisrael, the beginning of kedushah, had to start in Mitzrayim, and the Mashgiach suggests the same about the present galus in America. He closes with the Maharal on Rashi at the end of Noach: Avraham's tie to Terach was cut, as he began a new line.

catalogTitle: Lighting the Extinguished Candles

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach explains that Chanukah, a Yom Tov of the galus set in the darkest place and time, calls on every Jew to go out and relight the extinguished neshamos, while Hashem, behind the darkness, is preparing Moshiach.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with the idea of good and less good times: Jews prefer the first half of the month, when the moon grows, and the right side, the side of chesed. Chanukah breaks every rule: it falls at the end of the month, in the long nights of Teves, its lamp stands on the left of the door, below ten tefachim, out in the public domain. He explains that Chanukah and Purim are Yomim Tovim of the galus, and that the extinguished candles stand for the many neshamos blown out in the galus; Chanukah teaches a Jew to go out into the dark and relight them. He then takes up the questions people ask about the darkness of our time and answers them from the Midrash on 'Vayehi ba'eis hahi': while everyone was busy with his own troubles, Hashem was preparing the light of Moshiach. He closes by asking each listener to prepare himself and others for Moshiach, since every mitzvah lights more than one can see.

en: Jews prefer the first half of the month, when the moon waxes, and the right side of chesed, yet Chanukah falls at the end of the month and its lamp stands on the left side of the door.
Chanukah and Purim are Yomim Tovim of the galus, weekdays with a full Shemoneh Esrei, and Chanukah sits in the lowest place of the galus: end of the month, left side, the darkest nights of the year.
The extinguished candles are the neshamos blown out in the galus, and Chanukah teaches a Jew to go out into the public domain and relight them.
Behind the dark events of the parsha, and of our own time, Hashem is preparing Moshiach.
Every mitzvah is like a button whose effect a person cannot see, and lighting the Chanukah candle lights one's own neshamah and those of others.

title.en: Favorable times and the right side

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that there are favorable and unfavorable times, that the first half of the month is an eis ratzon because Jews are compared to the waxing moon, and that most Yomim Tovim fall on the first or fifteenth of the month. Chanukah is the exception, at the end of the month, and Jews also always give priority to the right side.

title.en: Chanukah in the lowest place of the galus

summary.en: The Mashgiach lists how Chanukah stands against the usual rules: its lamp is on the left side, at night in the long nights of Teves, in the public domain outside Hashem's 'atmosphere', and below ten tefachim where the Shechinah does not rest. He explains that Chanukah and Purim are weekday Yomim Tovim of the galus, and that Chanukah signifies the deepest galus.

title.en: Relighting the extinguished neshamos

summary.en: Using 'ner Hashem nishmas adam', the Mashgiach explains that many neshamos are blown out in the galus, and that on Chanukah a Jew goes out to the public domain to relight them. He says this is the darkest hour before dawn, and lists the questions people ask about the darkness of our time.

title.en: The troubles of the Avos and the light of Moshiach

summary.en: The Mashgiach asks why Yaakov Avinu had to bow to Esav, why Dina was taken, and why the brothers sold Yosef. He answers with the Midrash on 'Vayehi ba'eis hahi': while everyone was busy with his own matter, Hashem was preparing the light of Moshiach.

title.en: No free choice: everything leads to Moshiach

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings that the Shevatim had no free choice in selling Yosef, citing the Ohr HaChaim, and shows how Moshiach ben Yosef came from the episode of Dina and Moshiach ben David from Yehudah and Tamar, while the galus of Mitzrayim prepared the nation. He applies this to the confusing events of today.

title.en: Lighting your own neshamah and others'

summary.en: The Mashgiach tells his listeners to prepare themselves and others for Moshiach: lighting the Chanukah candle lights one's own neshamah, and like a button that lights a whole building, every mitzvah does more than one can see. He calls bringing light to the lost neshamos the task of this generation, and ends with a brachah.

catalogTitle: צד ב: אברהם אבינו ראש למאמינים

oneLiner.en: Following the Maharal's answer to the Ramban, the Mashgiach explains why Avraham Avinu's emunah was so great and why emunah, which frees a Jew from dependence on anyone but Hashem, is the foundation of Klal Yisrael.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with the Ramban's question on 'vehe'emin baShem': what was so praiseworthy in Avraham believing Hashem? The Maharal answers that by nature Avraham could not have children, and he feared sin might cancel the promise, yet he believed. From here the Mashgiach shows that a Jew's bond with Hashem does not rest on merits: the Torah gives no reason for 'Lech lecha', and the Ramban's 'great sin' of going down to Egypt teaches that a Jew remains a Jew and his sins are only external. He then follows the Maharal's challenge to the Ramban: emunah is no small thing, as the Mechilta's praise of the emunah at the sea shows. Emunah means firmness; a believer is subjugated to no person, as the Maharal's explanation of the dog shows. A believer is always joyful and never angry; Moshe's anger at Mei Merivah was a lack of emunah. He ends with Yaakov's 'me'ayin yavo ezri'.

en: According to the Maharal, Avraham's emunah was great because by nature he could not have children and he feared sin might cancel the promise, yet he believed because he saw that Hashem wanted it.
The Mashgiach teaches that a Jew's bond with Hashem does not depend on merits; this is why the Torah says 'Lech lecha' without first praising Avraham.
The first thing the Torah tells after 'Lech lecha' is what the Ramban calls Avraham's great sin, to show that a Jew remains a Jew even when he sins.
The Maharal argues against the Ramban that emunah is a great thing in itself, and Chazal say the Jews merited ruach hakodesh at the sea in reward for their emunah.
Emunah means firmness: a believer depends only on Hashem and is subjugated to no person, and the Jews left Egypt through emunah because it made them free.
One who believes in Hashem is always in simcha and does not become angry, and Moshe's anger at the rock was a lack of emunah.
